No fragment shows true implementations for helpers that report not supported here, nor their normal error or success paths.
No fragment shows synchronization for maps, links, tokens, keys or crypto beyond the sleepable array walk.

findings.text: The iterator feature enumeration provides a reschedule flag occupying bit zero.
The maximum count of context argument descriptors for an iterator registration is two.

Iterator registration carries a target name, attach and detach handlers, display and link information handlers, a prototype lookup handler, a descriptor size, a feature mask, a fixed small array of context argument helpers and a pointer to sequence information.
Iterator metadata carries a sequence file reference together with session and sequence counters.
Map element iteration context carries references to metadata and map plus opaque key and value pointers.
The immediate call argument helper ignores its index and always reports zero.
Map NUMA selection returns the attribute node when BPF_F_NUMA_NODE is present and otherwise reports no node.
Tracing context access is allowed only for non-negative offsets inside the argument area, for read type, and for naturally aligned sizes.
Typed tracing context access first applies the generic tracing checks and then delegates to BTF validation.
Core resolution context holds a verifier log pointer and a BTF pointer.
Unprivileged enablement has two configurations: one reflects negated sysctl_unprivileged_bpf_disabled and the other always reports disabled.
Current context presence has two configurations: one tests whether the current task carries a context pointer and the other always reports absent.
A sleepable array runner executes a list of programs against a shared context through a caller supplied runner and returns a combined status.

A null array yields success, zero length entries are skipped, recursion misses are counted and skipped, per item cookies are installed for each execution, and individual results are combined by logical conjunction starting from success.
The array walk disables migration for its whole duration and holds a read side guard only around execution of non sleepable entries while sleepable entries run without that guard.
Single miss accounting is a no operation in this configuration and the array wide helper walks entries until a null program while invoking the single accounting step and tolerating a null array.

Program lookup by descriptor, by type with or without driver binding, by path and by identifier, plus conditional reference acquisition, all fail with a not supported error marker in this configuration, and typed lookup without driver binding delegates to the driver aware form with binding disabled.
Program and map reference adjustments including add, subtract, increment and release are no operations in this configuration.

Link initialization for normal, sleepable and trampoline forms plus cleanup and unconditional release are no operations, priming and settling fail as not supported, object retrieval by user path fails as not supported, unconditional increment is a no operation, and conditional increment reports absence.
Token increment and release plus device and CPU flush list handling are no operations, while token lookup from descriptor and token information retrieval fail as not supported.
Cross device enqueue, device map enqueue for single and multi destination, generic redirect for device map and CPU map enqueue all report success without action in this configuration.
CPU map generic redirect and all program test executions for data path, tracing, dissector, socket lookup and system call report not supported, and structured type access reports access denied.

Base helper prototype lookup and just in time kernel function model lookup report absence, kernel function address lookup reports not supported, and task and control group storage release are no operations.
Dynamic pointer initialization, nulling and read only marking plus arena violation reporting and instruction pointer updating are no operations in this configuration.
Network capability is granted when CAP_NET_ADMIN or CAP_SYS_ADMIN privilege is present.
Kernel probe reading attempts a fault free copy when event support is enabled and otherwise starts from failure, returning the copy status.
On copy failure the destination is cleared to zeros, preventing stale or partial kernel bytes from reaching the caller.

Device binding and offload predicates have enabled forms that inspect auxiliary binding flags or compare map operations against the offload table with an unlikeliness hint, and disabled forms that always report false, while program pair matching always reports false.

Device bound validation, program initialization and inheritance report not supported, kernel function resolution reports absence, device unregistration and map release are no operations, offload map allocation reports not supported, and offload memory usage reports zero.
Socket map retrieval and query report invalid argument while detach, element update and link creation report not supported.
Socket reuseport detach is a no operation while file descriptor array element lookup and update report not supported.
Key wrapper holds a kernel key pointer and a flag recording whether a reference is held.

User and system key lookup report absence, key release is a no operation, signature verification reports not supported, and serial reporting has an enabled form returning the serial only when a reference is held and otherwise zero plus a disabled form always returning zero.
Common and plain socket context validation always deny, socket context conversion always yields zero, and read only dynamic pointer creation from socket buffers reports not supported.
Reuseport kernel state carries packet and socket references including selected and migrating sockets, a data end marker, hash and identifier values and a flag for wildcard binding.
Transmission control and express data path socket context validation always deny and their context conversion always yields zero.
Text patching distinguishes no operation, call and jump kinds.
Formatted output limits are twelve variable arguments, one thousand twenty four bytes of text buffer and five hundred twelve bytes of binary arguments.
Print buffers provide fixed storage for binary arguments and text, while print data holds pointers to those areas plus flags recording which area was requested.
Streaming helpers provide print and stack dump conveniences and a staging wrapper that prepares state, runs caller logic, commits for a program and stream, then releases state.
Control group attachment type acquisition and release are no operations.
Allocation type testing checks MEM_ALLOC, memory control flags add accounting when BPF memory control is enabled, and subprogram testing checks for a non zero function index.
Line information source holds file and line text pointers, a file name offset and numeric line and column positions.

Per CPU determination is true only for four per CPU map kinds, and operation flag checking rejects unknown low bits, lock use without a spin lock field, stray high bits without CPU selection, CPU selectors on non per CPU maps, combined CPU selectors, and out of range or impossible CPUs, with invalid argument or out of range errors.
Cryptographic type descriptor carries lifecycle, capability, keying, authentication size, cipher, size query and flag operations plus an owner reference and a short name.
Each header defines its own inclusion guard macro to prevent repeated inclusion.
Arena page fault handling always reports unhandled.
The hook macro declares a Linux Security Module hook implementation with a BPF prefix derived from the given name.
Storage blob holds a read copy update protected pointer to local storage.
Inode storage lookup returns absence when security data is missing and otherwise offsets into it by the inode storage size.
